# Plugin Conformance

The conformance gate is mandatory for every free plugin: manifest v2 is the only schema in this repo. A `free/` directory whose `plugin.json` is missing or is not `manifest_version: 2` fails the gate, and the `validate.yml` workflow runs it with `--all` on every pull request and push. There is no v1 path and no waiver for a plugin that cannot pass: it converts, or it leaves `free/`. The hand-kept registry JSON Schema is gone; `registry.json` is a projection generated by `tools/catalog`, and `plugin-counts.yml` fails when a committed file differs from the generator. Three codemods convert a v1 plugin, and an oracle proves that the released CLI v1.4.12 still installs the converted result.

## Run the gate

```bash
bash scripts/conformance/check.sh --plugins nself-foo,nself-bar   # named plugins
bash scripts/conformance/check.sh --changed                        # plugins changed against origin/main
bash scripts/conformance/check.sh --all                            # every plugin under free/ (also the default with no mode)
bash scripts/conformance/check.sh --fixtures                       # proves the gate itself (see below)
bash scripts/conformance/check.sh --plugins x --rules schema,compat   # a subset; only those rules run
bash scripts/conformance/check.sh --plugins x --migration-base DIR    # compare migrations with DIR/<plugin> trees
```

`migration-immutable` and `migration-idempotent` compare each plugin with its last release. By default the gate resolves the last `v*` tag (`git describe`; CI needs `fetch-depth: 0` or fetched tags), extracts `free/` from it with `git archive` into the work directory and prints `migration baseline: <tag>`. No tag fails the gate. `--migration-base DIR` uses DIR instead; it must hold `<plugin>/plugin.json` trees, and a directory that does not fails the gate rather than making every plugin look unreleased. A baseline `plugin.json` that exists but is not valid JSON fails both rules (it cannot be told apart from "not released" otherwise).

Exit 0 means every selected rule passed. A rule that cannot run (no Docker, no tool) fails; nothing passes by being skipped. A named plugin that does not exist fails, a plugin that is not manifest v2 fails (`FAIL manifest <plugin>`), and `--plugins` or `--all` that checks no plugin fails too (a gate that ran nothing is not a pass). Only `--changed` with nothing changed passes.

## Rules

| Rule | What it requires |
|---|---|
| `exceptions` | Every entry in `scripts/conformance/exceptions.yaml` is complete, expires on or before the v1.5.0 cap date and has not expired. |
| `schema` | `plugin.json` validates against the pinned v2 schema `schemas/plugin-manifest.v2.schema.json`. |
| `compat` | The manifest is canonical v2, has no forbidden v1 key, and the generated compatibility keys equal what `manifestv2migrate` projects. |
| `healthcheck` | A compose plugin has a real health check: a compose `healthcheck:` that is not disabled (`disable: true`, `test: NONE`), or a Dockerfile `HEALTHCHECK` whose last instruction is not `NONE`. A disabled compose healthcheck fails even when the Dockerfile has one. |
| `replace` | No `go.mod` or `go.work` `replace` or `use` points outside the plugin directory, quoted targets included. |
| `docker-socket` | No `docker.sock`, `/var/run/docker` or `/var/run` bind in the compose fragment named by `service.compose` (whatever it is called), in any `*.yml` or `*.yaml` of the plugin, or in a Dockerfile (ADR 0027), unless a dated exception names the plugin. |
| `port-bind` | Every published port of every compose service binds `127.0.0.1`: in the `service.compose` fragment (which must parse) and in any other `*.yml` or `*.yaml` of the plugin (outside `vendor/`, `node_modules/`, `third_party/` and `testdata/`) that has a top-level `services:` map. The parser is `scripts/conformance/portbind` (Go). A port with no host IP (`"9007:9007"`, `"9007"`), `0.0.0.0`, an IPv6 address, a host IP taken from a variable, a long-syntax entry without `host_ip: 127.0.0.1` and `network_mode: host` all fail. A deliberate public port is listed in `scripts/conformance/public-ports.yaml` (plugin, one container port, reason; no expiry; checked per port, so every other port of that plugin still has to bind `127.0.0.1`; `network_mode: host` is never excused). Today: `traefik` 80, 443 and 8444. The `exceptions` rule validates the file. A dated `port-bind` exception in `exceptions.yaml` still excuses a whole plugin. |
| `migrations` | A plugin with `migrations/*.sql` declares `migrations.apply: boot`, and a Go plugin calls `migrate.Apply` at boot in non-test source: a call in a comment or only in a `_test.go` file does not count. |
| `boot-schema` | A manifest with `migrations.apply: boot` declares `schema: np_<name with - replaced by _>`, the schema that holds its boot ledger. A `Schema: "np_..."` literal in non-test Go source must name the same schema. |
| `migration-immutable` | A boot migration file that the last release shipped is frozen: editing, deleting or renaming it fails, because the boot ledger stores each applied file's sha256 and a changed file is fatal at boot. Only plugins that the baseline release already applied at boot (manifest v2 with `migrations.apply: boot` at that tag) are checked; earlier releases had no ledger. Fix: add a new file. |
| `migration-idempotent` | Every boot migration that can still be applied for the first time is safe to replay (`IF NOT EXISTS`, `OR REPLACE`, guarded `DO` blocks, `ON CONFLICT`, ...; `UPDATE`, `DELETE` and `TRUNCATE` fail unless guarded in a `DO` block or excepted), because `plugin remove` drops the ledger but keeps the tables. Checked: files not in the baseline when the baseline plugin was boot-applied, otherwise all files. A real exception names the file and statement in `exceptions.yaml`. Guards in `DO` blocks are per branch: an `IF`/`ELSIF` branch whose own condition probes the catalog (`EXISTS (..)`, `to_regclass`, `pg_*`) covers a statement that mentions the probed object when the polarity fits (a statement that creates needs a "missing" probe, one that drops or alters needs an "exists" probe); an `ELSE`, loop or `CASE` branch is not covered, and an early `IF <probe> THEN RETURN` clause covers the statements after it the same way. An `EXCEPTION` handler protects the block only when a `WHEN` clause catches the replay error (`duplicate_*`, `undefined_*`, `OTHERS`, a matching `SQLSTATE`) and does not re-raise it. Each `INSERT` needs its own `ON CONFLICT` or a `NOT EXISTS` that reads its target table. Dynamic table renames must use `format('ALTER TABLE .. RENAME TO ..', r.old, r.new)` over a `FOR r IN SELECT old, new FROM (VALUES ('a', 'b'), ..) AS v(old, new)` list (or literal arguments). |
| `legacy-renames` | The table renames the boot migrations perform (literal `ALTER TABLE ... RENAME TO`, or a `DO` block renaming through a `VALUES` list; an unreadable rename fails) equal the `old new` lines of `tests/boot/legacy-renames`, and the Go `legacyTables` list when there is one. `tests/boot/legacy-probe.sql` holds SQL that `tests/boot/tables-upgrade.sh` runs on the legacy database after the converted boot; a probe without `legacy-renames` would never run, so it fails. A plugin with no renames and no fixture passes. |
| `repository` | A free manifest names `https://github.com/nself-org/plugins`; a licensed one names `https://github.com/nself-org/bundles`. |
| `ports` | No port is shared by two plugins or claimed from `scripts/conformance/reserved-ports.yaml`. |
| `build` | The plugin builds from its own extracted deterministic tarball with no network (`build-from-tarball.sh`). |

`ports.sh` reads the top-level `port`, `config.port`, `service.port` and every `*_PORT` default under the optional env of each manifest. `ports.sh --all --report` lists collisions among all current plugins (legacy v1 included) and exits 0.

## Exceptions

`scripts/conformance/exceptions.yaml` lists the only allowed rule breaks. Each entry has `rule`, `plugin`, `reason`, `owner_ref` and `expires`. An expired entry fails the gate, and `expires` may not be later than the v1.5.0 cap date. The cap is a constant in `scripts/conformance/lib.sh` (`release_cap`), not read from the data file, so a file cannot raise its own cap. Remove an entry in the same change that lands its owner Ticket. Today: `docker-socket` for `forgejo` and `monitoring`, and `cli-targets` entries for plugins whose release builds no binary yet (see the file).

## Pinned schema

The schema copy is pulled, never edited. `scripts/cli-tools.version` pins the `nself-org/cli` commit that holds `tools/manifestv2migrate`, the schema and `sdk/go/migrate`. `sync-schema.sh` copies the schema from that commit and records its sha256 in `schemas/SOURCE`; `sync-schema.sh --check` fails on any mismatch. To move the pin, change the sha, then run `sync-schema.sh`.

## Codemods

All three are idempotent: a second run reports `noop` and changes nothing. Each plugin is converted as ONE all-or-nothing unit: `run.sh` snapshots the plugin directory and restores it exactly if any step fails or is manual, and each script restores its own writes on failure. Boot and vendor run only after the manifest step converted (or was already a no-op); a plugin whose manifest is blocked or manual is not touched.

```bash
bash scripts/codemods/run.sh --plugins nself-foo            # convert in place
bash scripts/codemods/run.sh --dry-run --all --report r.txt # per-plugin report and summary, writes nothing
bash scripts/codemods/run.sh --fixtures --twice             # prove them on tests/conformance/fixtures
bash tests/conformance/realtree.sh --drop-dev-tool-keys --plugins a,b   # idempotence on the real free/ tree (twice, zero changes)
```

| Codemod | Does |
|---|---|
| `manifest-v2.sh` | Runs `manifestv2migrate` with compatibility keys, sets `repository` on free manifests, drops the dead keys in the cli drop list. Keys that plugins dev tools still read (`dev-tool-keys.txt`: actions, config, binary_name, env_required, env_optional, defaultPort) are KEPT, so a manifest carrying one reports `blocked: <keys>` and nothing is written, until a Ticket whose scope updates the readers passes `--drop-dev-tool-keys`. A v1 key that is neither mapped nor on a drop list also blocks. A converted manifest whose `service.compose` fragment does not exist reports `manual` and is not written. |
| `vendor.sh` | Copies out-of-dir `replace` targets into `third_party/`, runs `go mod vendor` for the plugin's own modules (not `third_party/`, not a module reached through a local replace), adds `-mod=vendor` to the Dockerfile build. A Dockerfile that runs `go mod download` reports `manual` before anything is written. |
| `boot-migrations.sh` | For a Go plugin with `migrations/`: `migrations.apply: boot`, a `go:embed` package, one `Apply` call after the pgx pool is created, a `/health` migrations member, and the SDK module copied under `third_party/cli-sdk-go` with its LICENSE and tidy `go.mod`/`go.sum`. A plugin with more than one `go.mod`, or whose pool pattern is not found, reports `manual` and nothing is written. |

`run.sh` prints one `plugin <name> manifest=<s> boot=<s> vendor=<s>` line per plugin and ends with `summary` lines (counts per step and the blocked and manual plugin lists). States: `converted`, `noop`, `none` (nothing to do), `manual` (needs hand wiring), `blocked` (unmapped key, failed step) and `skipped`. Outside `--dry-run` a blocked plugin makes the run exit 1; a dry run always exits 0 because the report is its product.

## Fresh-database boot kit

`bash tests/boot/run.sh --fixtures` builds each converted fixture image, starts `postgres:16`, boots the plugin twice and requires: the first boot applies every migration, the second applies none, and `/health` reports `applied == expected`. Use `--plugins a,b` for real plugins and `--sequential` on small machines.

## v1.4.12 oracle

`bash scripts/conformance/v14-oracle.sh --fixtures` runs its container as the host uid (`--user`), so the files it writes into the work directory are readable by the host user on native Linux. It downloads the `nself` v1.4.12 linux release (nothing else), verifies its sha256 against the release `checksums.txt`, then in a container with no network installs each plugin twice from a local registry: once as its v1 original, once converted. It diffs the generated compose, `compose-files.txt`, the `PLUGIN_*_INTERNAL_URL` lines in `.nself/compose.env`, the `np_plugins` seed SQL, `plugin list --installed --detailed` and the `plugin remove` guard on a depended-on plugin. Any difference fails unless `tests/conformance/oracle-deltas.yaml` lists it (`slug`, `file`, `key`, `from`, `to`, `owner_ref`, `expires`). A row matches literally (never a regex), only in its own output file, and only for a plugin under test: `from: "-"` removes only a converted-side line exactly equal to `key`; otherwise lines containing `key` have `to` replaced by `from`. A row that matches nothing while its plugin is under test is stale and fails, an expired row fails, and an `expires` after the v1.5.0 cap (a constant in `lib.sh`) fails. `tests/conformance/oracle-deltas-test.sh` holds the negative proofs. With `--plugins a,b` the originals come from `origin/main`.

Known difference: v1.4.12 parses `dependencies` only as an array. The object form `{required, optional}` used by most free manifests makes it skip that plugin when it wires `PLUGIN_<DEP>_INTERNAL_URL`, so the converted twin gains the line. The delta rows for the fixtures document it.

## Proofs that the gate works

`check.sh --fixtures` converts the v1 fixtures, requires the gate to pass on them, then plants each defect on a copy (legacy key, bad enum, compatibility drift, missing healthcheck, `HEALTHCHECK NONE`, disabled healthcheck, out-of-dir replace incl. quoted and `go.work` forms, unapplied migration, unwired migration, `migrate.Apply` only in a comment or a test file, wrong repository, docker socket without an exception incl. in the `service.compose` fragment and other yaml files, a port published beyond loopback (no host IP, `0.0.0.0`, `[::]`, a host IP from a variable, long syntax without `host_ip`, a flow list, another compose file, a renamed fragment, `network_mode: host`), a boot-migration plugin without its `np_` schema, with a different one, or whose Go boot code names another schema, an edited or deleted released migration, a new non-idempotent migration (plain index, insert, update, constraint, unguarded `EXECUTE`), a malformed baseline manifest, a rename without its `legacy-renames` fixture or with the wrong pair, a `legacy-probe.sql` without `legacy-renames`, a bad `--migration-base`, unvendored build, expired exception, an exception that raises its own cap, a gate that checks no plugin, a planted v1 manifest, a plugin directory with no `plugin.json`) and requires the named rule to fail. It also requires the matching good cases to pass: a loopback long-syntax port, a Kubernetes yaml with `containerPort`, a port with an unexpired exception, guarded new migrations and renames with their fixture. The `conformance` job in `.github/workflows/validate.yml` runs the gate on every free plugin (`--all`), `tests/manifests/validate-free-manifests.sh` (every free manifest against manifest v2) and all of these proofs on every pull request.
